elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Type II Materials — expressly including materials "created during the Service performance period" — remain those "in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)". Only Type I Materials vest in Customer, so ownership of deliverables generally is not with Customer.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language from IBM to Customer appears anywhere in the rendered text; Customer's rights in Type II Materials rest solely on a licence back.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "Type II Materials are those, created during the Service performance period or otherwise (such as those that preexist the Service), in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 renders: "IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, paid-up license..." covering Type II (IBM-owned) Materials delivered to Customer.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, paid-up license" (irrevocable retained from the original grant).

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" added alongside the retained "paid-up" in the Type II grant.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: No operative sentence affirms Customer's ownership of or retained rights in Customer Data; § 14.18 as amended only limits IBM's permitted use of contact information and still states "Your contact information shall not be considered personal information processed on your behalf." A Customer Data ownership sentence would need to be inserted.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Operation 2: "Such information will be stored, processed and used solely to provide the Services, and may be provided to contractors ... solely for that purpose", deleting the prior business-relationship, Business Partner/assignee, promotion and marketing-research uses.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the Materials scheme allocates each category exclusively (Type I to Customer, Type II to IBM/third parties); no joint-ownership language exists to delete.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Retained: Type II Materials, including those that "preexist the Service", are those "in which IBM or third parties have all right, title, and interest (including ownership of copyright)"; the redline leaves IBM's ownership untouched.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Rendered grant now reads "a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, paid-up license" — "perpetual" added by operation 1.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "irrevocable" retained in the Type II grant to Customer.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" retained in the Type II grant to Customer.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" expressly added; the retained "paid-up" is pre-existing favourable language rather than a substitute.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify, execute, reproduce, display, perform, distribute and sublicense, for Customer's business purposes, copies of Type II Materials" — the prior "within Customer's Enterprise only" limit is replaced.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "...distribute and sublicense, for Customer's business purposes, copies of Type II Materials."

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Amended § 14.18: information "will be stored, processed and used solely to provide the Services", onward provision limited to contractors "solely for that purpose"; Business Partners, assignees, promotion and marketing-research uses removed.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all eight fallback elements are met in the rendered operative language — IBM keeps ownership of Type II/pre-existing Materials, and the licence back is now perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and permits use, modification, distribution and sublicensing for Customer's business purposes; § 14.18 confines IBM's use of Customer contact data to providing the Services.

Preferred is not complete: there is no assignment of deliverables/work product to Customer (Type II Materials created during performance remain IBM-owned) and no operative sentence stating that Customer retains all rights in Customer Data. To reach preferred the drafter would need (i) an express IBM assignment of deliverables and work product created for Customer, and (ii) a Customer Data ownership sentence.

Minimality holds: operation 1 edits only the licence attributes and scope words in the Type II grant and retains the favourable existing terms ("irrevocable", "worldwide", "nonexclusive", "paid-up"); operation 2 deletes only the exploitation purposes and recipients (Business Partners, assignees, promotion, marketing research) needed to reach the Customer Data element. Adding "stored" is within the target element because the preceding retained sentence otherwise permits unrestricted storage "anywhere they do business". No survival tails, expense language or extraneous procedures were added.

Intent is preserved: the two-category Materials structure, IBM's delivery obligation, the Type I allocation and the data-protection/instructions sentences all survive without contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created. Correctly, no new IBM-side exception or grant was introduced.

Residual (correctly noted as outside this checklist, not a defect here): the Type I licence back to IBM in p0084 permits external distribution, derivative works and authorising others in Customer-owned Materials; if Type I Materials could in practice carry Customer Data, that grant would need narrowing under the same element.
